name: Federalism
summary: Federalism holds that political authority should be divided between a central government and regional governments, each with powers the other cannot simply take away, usually set out in a written constitution. Adherents argue this restrains tyranny, lets diverse communities govern themselves, and keeps a large state together. It is a structural doctrine and has no fixed position on economic or social policy.
scope: Mainstream constitutional federalism as described in Wikipedia and the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, drawing on Madison and Hamilton (Federalist Nos. 39 and 51), Montesquieu, Althusius and Mill. Covers both coming-together (US, Switzerland) and holding-together (India, Belgium) federations. Excludes anarchist federalism (Proudhon), and the specific US Federalist Party and states-rights politics. Because it is a form of government, most policy answers are neutral and low confidence.

keyFigures.name: James Madison
keyFigures.role: Principal author of the US Constitution and of Federalist essays defending the federal design.

keyFigures.name: Johannes Althusius
keyFigures.role: Early modern thinker named as a father of modern federalism.

keyFigures.name: Montesquieu
keyFigures.role: Advocated confederate republics combining the benefits of small and large states.

sources.usedFor: Justifications (liberty, diversity, democracy), secession, courts, fiscal and multinational federalism, subsidiarity.

strong-leader.rationale: Federalists build checks and divided power precisely to stop a single authority bypassing others.

state-harmful.rationale: Federalism is a way of organizing the state, with two levels of government, not abolishing it (anarchist federalism is a separate strand).

decide-locally.rationale: Federalism divides powers so regional governments handle regional matters, and subsidiarity is a related principle; yet defence, foreign policy and common rules stay central, so it is not "as local as possible".

gradual-change.rationale: Federal constitutions are typically hard to amend, but federalism is not about the pace of social change.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Federalists split: some advocate supranational federations such as the EU, others stress national and regional authority.

revolution-justified.rationale: Federalists present divided power as a way to reduce tyranny, rebellion and war; mainstream adherents prefer constitutional means.

one-party-rule.rationale: Divided and competing centres of power are the point of federalism; single-party control cuts against it.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Federations include monarchies (Canada, Australia) and republics; the ideology is indifferent.

democracy-best.rationale: Madison defends the federal plan as republican, with power derived from the people; federalism is usually paired with democratic government.

direct-votes.rationale: Federal systems often include referendums (Switzerland) but federalism does not require them.

workers-councils.rationale: Mainstream federalism works through constitutional legislatures; anarchist federalism is a different strand.

right-to-secede.rationale: A federation is distinguished from a confederation partly by lacking a unilateral right of exit; federalists treat autonomy as the alternative to secession.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Federalism is commonly adopted to accommodate culturally and ethnically diverse societies in one state.

total-state.rationale: Dividing authority between levels and guarding it by constitution limits any state directing all life.

national-self-determination.rationale: Federalism accommodates national minorities within a state, but adherents differ on whether each nation needs its own state.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Federalists distrust concentrated power but do not hold elites uniformly corrupt.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Federalist 39 grounds the constitution in ratification by the people acting through their states.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Federal constitutions differ (Germany bans such parties, the US does not), and the doctrine itself does not settle it.

separated-powers.rationale: Madison argues that dividing power between levels and branches gives a double security to the rights of the people.

priority-to-poor.rationale: A form-of-government doctrine, compatible with both left and right social policy.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The Stanford entry lists accommodating diversity as a main justification for federalism, so adherents do not treat diversity as a threat to cohesion.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Madison's checks and double security favour dividing and separating powers over concentrating them in one head.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Federalism is silent on censorship; adherents differ.

recall-officials.rationale: Federalism is silent on recall; Madison favoured representative over direct mechanisms but adherents vary.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Federalism protects regional diversity but takes no view on ranking cultures; adherents differ.

death-penalty.rationale: Federalism lets regions choose their own penal policy but takes no position on capital punishment itself.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Madison's concern for minority rights and Mill's liberty point toward tolerance, but federalism takes no view on custom versus eccentricity.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Federations are often founded by conventions or assemblies, but federalism sets no rule for how constitutions are rewritten, so adherents are split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Federations differ on this, from partisan presidents (US) to ceremonial non-party heads (Germany), and the doctrine itself takes no side.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Federal constitutions differ on whether member units may leave, and adherents are split between holding-together and voluntary-union views.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Guaranteed regional self-rule with its own laws is the core of federal design, and asymmetric arrangements that let one region keep distinct institutions are an accepted federal variant.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Federalism is a structural doctrine with no position on tax design; adherents hold varied views.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Federalist No. 51 and the whole design of divided and checked power aim to bind rulers by constitutional limits, so an unbound sovereign contradicts the doctrine.

space-expansion.rationale: Unrelated to the division of powers; adherents hold varied views.

equal-parenting.rationale: A family-law question outside the doctrine's scope; adherents differ.

land-redistribution.rationale: Structural doctrine with no position on land policy; federations differ.

common-currency.rationale: Federations differ on currency union; adherents are split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Federalism is described as letting diverse communities self-govern within one state, including holding-together federations for national minorities.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Structural doctrine; Federalist authors argue from institutions and ambition, not economic forces.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Federalist No. 51 and the written-constitution model rest on checks that limit majorities.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Federalist No. 39 grounds republican government in the people rather than hereditary power.

elective-rulers.rationale: Federal systems exist as both republics and monarchies (for example Canada and Belgium), so the doctrine does not settle how rulers are chosen.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The statement contrasts parliament with a monarch, a question federal theory does not settle; federalism subordinates every legislature to the constitution, which the statement does not ask about.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A historical question that the doctrine does not decide.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Federalism values diversity but is itself offered as a widely applicable design, so it does not settle this.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Madison's design relies on representatives exercising judgment under checks and fixed terms, not on binding instructions and instant recall.

single-official-language.rationale: Federalism is justified partly by accommodating regional diversity, so imposing one language over others sits poorly with it.

corporate-influence.rationale: A structural doctrine that is silent on lobbying; adherents are split.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Federalism is silent on funding rules; adherents vary.

job-guarantee.rationale: Federalism is silent on employment policy; adherents take varied positions.

democratic-peace.rationale: Federalism does not address this claim; adherents are split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Federalism rests on constitutional law and consent, so adherents lean against a view that denies any general duty of obedience.

local-production.rationale: Subsidiarity favours local decisions but not necessarily local production; adherents are split.

informal-organisation.rationale: Federalism is built on permanent constitutional institutions and levels of government, which sits against purely informal organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Adherents are split: US-style federalists stress constitutional supremacy, while European federalists favour supranational law.

religious-nation.rationale: Federalism is meant to hold diverse communities together, so defining the nation by one religion cuts against it.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Federalism concerns internal division of power and is silent on relations between states; its adherents take varied positions.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Doctrine is silent on fiscal sharing; federal systems differ between equalisation and regional retention, and adherents are split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Federalism is a structural doctrine and silent on property; adherents take varied positions.

defeat-communism.rationale: Federalism is silent on foreign and ideological conflict; adherents take varied positions.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Federalism is silent on how services are delivered; adherents take varied positions.

religion-illusion.rationale: Federalism is silent on religion; adherents take varied positions.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Federalism is silent on economic history; adherents take varied positions.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Federalism is silent on gender and economics; adherents take varied positions.

socialized-care.rationale: Federalism is silent on domestic and care work; adherents take varied positions.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Federalism is silent on language policy; federations often protect regional languages, but adherents differ on a national language.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Federalism keeps a constitutional order of divided governments rather than replacing it with communal societies.

majority-settlement.rationale: Federalism protects regional self-rule, including of minority-majority regions, so state-steered majority settlement cuts against its principles.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Federalism is silent on economic systems; adherents take varied positions.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Federalism concerns the division of power, not rival land claims; it can serve claims of either kind.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Federalism lets sub-units decide such matters, and adherents take varied positions.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Madison's Federalist 51 grounds the division of power in checking tyranny and protecting minorities, which suppressing opposition would undermine.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Federalism leaves religion to the constitution's division of powers; adherents differ.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Federalism lets states or regions decide such rights, and federal adherents split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Federalism allows sub-units to differ on such questions, and adherents split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Federalism concerns the structure of government and is compatible with any political side.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Federalism lets regions decide such rules, so adherents are split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Federalism concerns dividing power between levels of government and is silent on succession; federations include monarchies such as Belgium and Canada, so adherents split.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Federalism is silent on this; adherents hold varied views on international lenders.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Federalism concerns dividing power between levels of government and is silent on sortition; Madison favoured representation, but adherents vary and some federations use citizens' assemblies.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Federalism is a constitutional form that takes no position on religious doctrine, and its adherents vary widely.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Federalism is itself a way of sharing power between territorial communities rather than leaving it to a simple national majority, as in Switzerland and Belgium.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Subsidiarity favours handling matters at the lowest competent level, but federalism does not say whether that level is government or charity; adherents split.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Federalism is silent on religious office; adherents hold varied views.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Federalism is silent on family authority; adherents hold varied views.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Federalism lets constituent units set their own local rules, and some federations (such as Swiss cantons) let foreign residents vote locally, but the doctrine does not require it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Federalism is a structure for dividing authority and leaves defence and foreign basing to the policies of each federation.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Federalism is about dividing power and does not require any view of national origins; its diversity-friendly adherents tend to avoid single-origin claims.

culture-before-state.rationale: Federalism does not rank cultural renewal against state-building.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Federalism says which level decides, not whether services are public; subsidiarity places such services at the lower level.

second-chamber.rationale: Federal systems usually add a chamber representing the member states, as in the US Senate that Federalist No. 39 describes as federal in character; this is common rather than essential.

municipal-property.rationale: Federalism is neutral on property, and its constitutional tradition (Madison) accepts private property; community ownership is not part of it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Federalists distinguish a federation, where the centre acts directly on citizens, from a confederation of delegates; Federalist No. 39 treats the latter as weaker.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The defining feature is that regional and central governments each have powers the other cannot remove, as Federalist No. 39 and the scholarship describe; revocable powers describe devolution, not federalism.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Mainstream federalism divides power by territory and constitution, not by race; Madison's Federalist No. 51 aims at protecting minorities by structure, not by racial organisation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Federalism is a division of power between levels, and adherents split on whether communal electorates fit it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Federalism is silent on environmental tools; adherents take varied positions.

arms-reduction.rationale: Federalism is silent on arms; foreign and defence powers are usually central but adherents hold varied views.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Federalism is silent on diplomatic secrecy; Madison defended some confidentiality in the Constitutional Convention but this is not argued in the sources.

capital-controls.rationale: Federalism is silent on capital controls; adherents take varied positions.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Federalism divides power between levels of government and is silent on who may bear arms, though most federations leave the monopoly of force with the state; adherents are split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Federalism is silent on income top-ups, though it lets regions choose their own policies; adherents are split.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The sources discuss fiscal federalism and the division of taxing power but take no side on binding debt limits; adherents are split.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Federalism is silent on student debt and adherents hold varied positions.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Federalism recognises regional grievances in multinational and fiscal federations, but takes no position on exploitation between regions; adherents are split.

public-service-media.rationale: Federalism is silent on public broadcasting; adherents differ.

farm-price-support.rationale: Federalism is neutral on farm policy; it only allocates which level decides.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Neutral; defence powers usually go to the centre, but the doctrine takes no side on nuclear arms.

ban-fgm.rationale: Neutral; it concerns which level of government decides, not the substance.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Neutral on the substance of inheritance law.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Neutral on liability versus agency regulation; the doctrine only addresses which level decides.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Neutral; federations vary in whether customary authorities have a formal role.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Neutral on policy trade-offs; it only addresses the level of decision.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Neutral on sentencing policy; federalism allows levels to differ.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Neutral on the substance; federal systems differ on language rules.

voter-id.rationale: Federalism leaves election rules to whichever level holds that power, so adherents take varied positions on voter ID.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Federalism is silent on religion's legal standing, and federations differ on it.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Federalist sources justify the system by liberty and consent as well as elections, but do not settle how democracy should be defined.

premarital-sex.rationale: A structural doctrine with no view on sexual morality; federalists differ, and federalism would let regions decide.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Welfare design is not a federalist matter; the doctrine only asks which level should run it.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Federalism is silent on religion and gender; adherents split on the claim.

race-social-construct.rationale: This is outside federalism's concerns, and adherents hold varied views.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Federalism only asks at which level such agencies sit, so adherents take varied positions on having them at all.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Federalism concerns how power is divided between levels of government and is silent on how property is first owned.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Federalism is silent on international criminal justice; adherents take varied positions.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Federalism does not address gender equality in group self-rule; adherents' views vary.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Federalism does not address economic systems; adherents take varied positions.

indirect-election.rationale: Madison in Federalist 39 describes a Senate chosen by state legislatures as part of the federal form, though modern federations vary.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Stanford Encyclopedia describes multinational federalism as a way to give minority-majority regions self-rule within one state.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Federalism does not say who decides disputed territories; adherents are split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Federalism does not address settlement restrictions, though regions might set their own; adherents are split.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Federal constitutions entrench limits on every level of government, and killing without trial is incompatible with the rule-of-law restraints Madison's Federalist No. 51 builds on.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Tax policy is left open; federalism only concerns which level may tax, so adherents are split.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Federalism is silent on how welfare is designed; adherents vary, though it favours the level of government closest to recipients deciding.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Federalism is often used to give religious or ethnic communities self-rule, as in Belgium or India, but other federations are secular; adherents are split.

missingStatements.text: A national constitution should divide power between central and regional governments, each with powers the other cannot remove.
missingStatements.rationale: Constitutionally entrenched division of sovereignty is the defining feature of federal systems.

notes: Anarchist federalists and EU-style supranational federalists would answer several statements differently. Many answers are neutral because federalism is a form of government compatible with left and right policy.
